models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.why: On Strix Halo the runtime decides everything: a Vulkan llama.cpp build with the open DFlash 2 pull request (PR #27342) roughly doubles decode at 32K context on the same Ryzen AI Max+ 395, and a portable 'Vulcan' build reaches ~33 tok/s shared across four lanes on a 128GB box.

engines.quant: llama.cpp + Vulkan, Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL + DFlash2 drafter Q8_0 (n=4); 26.39 tok/s at 0K context (21.58 at 8K, 21.11 at 32K) vs 11.81 baseline — needs llama.cpp PR #27342
PCIE_VULKAN build, Q3_K_XL, 64K context, vision enabled; ~33 tok/s shared across four concurrent lanes

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B
models.why: Experimental Strix Halo support in Strata keeps a 125B MoE decoding at 27 tok/s from 168K to 262K context on a 16GB-VRAM + 96GB RAM laptop, and hits 55-58 tok/s in 140W Performance mode — quarter-million-token context on one APU.

engines.hardware: Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo laptop (Bosgame M5, 16GB VRAM + 96GB RAM)
engines.quant: Unsloth Q4 / GSQ-RCO weights, experimental Strix Halo support (Linux only); 27 tok/s at 168K-262K context in real work, 55-58 tok/s decode in 140W Performance mode
ROCm; the post reports ~40 tok/s for the model on the Strix Halo APU

models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
models.why: AMD day-0 support puts the 30B dense agentic model on both AMD shapes: a 4-bit quant brings the language model under 17-21GB, leaving room for KV cache, the vision encoder and a DFlash drafter in a 24/32GB envelope — up to ~24 tok/s on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 APU.

engines.hardware: Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo, unified memory)
engines.quant: 4-bit, Vulkan backend + DFlash speculative decoding, Windows 11 Pro 25H2, averaged over multiple runs (AMD day-0 blog)
engines.engine_min_version: llama.cpp with Vulkan backend and DFlash support
